items.title: New flights coming to international cities from Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Air Canada is planning new flights to Europe and Central America from Toronto Pearson International Airport in Mississauga starting next year. The airline made the announcement on Thursday that it will start flights to Oslo, Norway; Shannon, Ireland and Nice, France in the summer of 2027. The Oslo flights will be the airline’s third Scandinavian destination, with routes to Stockholm and Copenhagen, and will be the only North American non-stop flights to Norway. Flights to Oslo will be operated onboard its new Airbus A321XLR fleet featuring two cabins including the premium Air Canada Signature cabin with lie-flat seats. Flights have been scheduled to connect conveniently at its Toronto global hub to a multitude of destinations across North America. Air Canada’s upcoming plans also include the return of the Toronto to London-Heathrow Day-tripper service, daily Toronto-to-Shanghai trips and a new Toronto-to-Guatemala City flight launching this December that will run year-round. “The airline’s new service to Oslo, Shannon and Nice, along with enhanced connectivity to other key international destinations, strengthen vital links to global markets. Simply put, this gives passengers more choice,” said Deborah Flint, President and CEO of Toronto Pearson. Air Canada’s Oslo flights will be operated onboard its new Airbus A321XLR fleet featuring two cabins including the premium Air Canada Signature cabin with lie-flat seats. Thursday’s flight announcements will follow the addition of new services this winter from Toronto to Ecuador, Spain, and year-round operations to Manchester, Copenhagen and Denmark. Air Canada says services to Tenerife, Manchester and Copenhagen will also be operated on the new Airbus A321XLR aircraft. items.title: The Proud Canadian History of Lake Ontario
items.summary: THE RIDGETOWN IN LAKE ONTARIO. PHOTO BY JAY KANA. Over the years, we have often marked the end of the summer season with a Blue Rodeo concert at the RBC Amphitheatre in Toronto. The evening is always a summer highlight for us. This year’s concert created a special memory though, something that brought encouragement, reinforced personal resolve and created a feeling of solidarity amongst my fellow citizens and concert-goers, amidst these fractured economic and political times. Set against the backdrop of Lake Ontario, and with perspectives shaped by the news out of the United States of the “renaming” of the lake, Blue Rodeo performed their “Hasn’t Hit Me Yet” song towards the end of the evening. ” It was a spontaneous, clear and proudly Canadian moment. The name is, and will always be, for us, Lake Ontario. That moment led me to reflect on the history of the name – something that people who have lived along its shores have known and recorded for hundreds of years. For starters, to clarify the timeline, our province takes its name from the lake. What is now the Province of Ontario has been home to Indigenous peoples for thousands of years. In colonial terms, after 1608 the province was originally part of the Pays d’en Haut (“Upper Country”) area of New France. After the fall of New France and the Treaty of Paris in 1763, Great Britain reorganized the administration of New France as the Province (or colony) of Quebec. The Constitutional Act of 1791 split the Province of Quebec into Upper Canada (now Ontario) and Lower Canada (now Quebec).

items.title: Road safety crucial as kids go back to school in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Drivers and others are being reminded about road safety as neighbourhood streets in Mississauga are about to get much busier with young pedestrians, school buses and parents dropping off and picking up their kids. Early next week, tens of thousands of students will return to classes in Mississauga for the 2026-27 school year. Both the City of Mississauga and Peel Regional Police have similar messages for drivers as they travel in and near the many school zones across the city — slow down, watch for kids both on foot and on bicycles, and obey school bus signals and all traffic signs. “In the coming days, school zones, crossings and neighbourhood streets will become noticeably busier. The city is reminding drivers, transit users, cyclists, e-scooter users and pedestrians to be extra careful during the busy morning and afternoon school rush,” city officials said in an online reminder to the community on Thursday. “With increased traffic and activity on the road, the risk of collisions is higher. ” City officials and police note that streets, driveways and sidewalks around schools will quickly transform from relatively quiet areas during the summer to much busier spots as school bells ring starting on Sept. 8 — the day after Labour Day — to mark the start of a new academic year for students in Peel.

items.title: $401M from Ontario and Ottawa will help pay for major transit projects in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga officials say more than $401 million received on Thursday from the provincial and federal governments will help build “important new transit projects” and other infrastructure to pave the way for much-needed additional housing. 4 million in funding comes via the Development Charges Reduction Program, a joint initiative of the province and Ottawa that helps municipalities who’ve reduced development charges invest in infrastructure needed to support growth. City officials said Mississauga was one of the first cities in Ontario to substantially reduce, or in some cases eliminate altogether, development charges to help get more homes built and make them more affordable. Mississauga will maintain those reductions until March 31, 2029. “Mississauga acted early to help get more homes built and make them more affordable for our residents,” Mayor Carolyn Parrish said in a news release following Thursday’s surprise announcement in Mississauga, adding the funding received “demonstrates the value of that leadership. This significant investment from our government partners will help us deliver the infrastructure needed to support new homes in every neighbourhood. It will also help better connect residents and visitors to our downtown. ” Representatives from the city and both provincial and federal governments were on hand for the funding reveal, to which the media was not invited. ” The funding will help build more homes and community infrastructure in Mississauga “while advancing the province’s plan to protect Ontario by investing in projects that lower costs for families, support economic growth and keep workers on the job,” the province said.

items.title: Mississauga to receive up to $401.4 million to support housing and community infrastructure
items.summary: The City’s efforts to make it easier to build new homes, including significant development charge reductions, helped secure the substantial new funding. 4 million in funding to help Mississauga build housing-enabling infrastructure including important new transit projects. Mayor Carolyn Parrish and Members of Council joined Ontario Premier Doug Ford for today’s official announcement alongside Rob Flack, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Jennifer McKelvie, Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Housing and Infrastructure and Member of Parliament for Ajax, and Peter Fonseca, Member of Parliament for Mississauga-East Cooksville. The funding, part of the Development Charges Reduction Program, helps municipalities who have reduced development charges invest in the infrastructure they need to support growth. It is part of the broader Canada-Ontario Partnership to Build. Mississauga was one of the first cities in Ontario to substantially reduce development charges – by up to 100 per cent – to help get more homes built and make them more affordable. The City has agreed to maintain these reductions until March 31, 2029. The new funding will help support housing-enabling infrastructure including two key transit projects: a new zero-emissions transit maintenance and storage facility and new downtown transit mobility hub. As Canada’s seventh largest city, significant investment in transit infrastructure is critical to support new housing development. These investments, which the City has long advocated for, will help support Mississauga’s growing population and deliver lasting benefits for residents and businesses. The City is planning a new zero-emission transit facility on City-owned land at 7300 West Credit Avenue to support future growth and improve service.

items.title: Lakeview Home's $1.78 Million Over-Asking Sale Tops Mississauga's Market Last Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, a four-bedroom home in Mississauga's Lakeview neighbourhood was the city's most expensive over-asking sale last month, according to a new report from Zoocasa. The outlet reports the home sold for $1,782,777, well above its $1,699,000 list price. INsauga reports the property includes a mudroom with direct garage access, a built-in surround sound system, and a finished basement with a home theatre and wine cellar. According to the outlet, the backyard also features an in-ground pool. INsauga reports the sale was highlighted in Zoocasa's monthly roundup of the Greater Toronto Area's top over-asking home sales, drawing attention to Mississauga's competitive housing market.

items.title: Bromsgrove Road Reopens After Storm Flooding as Mississauga Fares Better Than Other Regions
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga saw flooding and downed trees during this week's severe storms, though the city fared better than several other Ontario regions hit harder by the system. The outlet reports Bromsgrove Road was temporarily closed between Southdown Road and Winston Churchill Boulevard due to flooding before reopening once water levels receded. INsauga reports Credit Valley Conservation has since downgraded its flood warnings for the area. A city spokesperson named McCutcheon told the outlet that Mississauga received a limited number of service requests related to flooding and downed trees compared with other municipalities. According to INsauga, city crews are continuing to assess parks and trails for storm damage in the aftermath of the system.

items.title: Erin Mills Parkway Tower Proposal Scaled Back Under Ontario Land Tribunal Settlement
items.summary: According to INsauga, a massive proposed development at 5100 Erin Mills Parkway has been scaled back under a settlement offer filed with the Ontario Land Tribunal. The outlet reports the original proposal called for nine towers ranging from 20 to 44 storeys with a total of 3,162 units. INsauga reports the revised plan reduces the tallest towers to a maximum of 37 storeys, with building heights across the site now ranging from 20 to 37 storeys depending on location. According to the outlet, only two of the buildings still exceed the 25-storey maximum allowed under the city's Official Plan, down from five buildings in the original proposal. INsauga reports the settlement also relocates a 4,206-square-metre park to the northwest corner of the site.

items.title: Ottawa and Ontario Unveil Development Charges Program Aimed at Mississauga Home Affordability
items.summary: According to a joint announcement covered by Yahoo Finance Canada, the federal and Ontario governments say a new Development Charges Reduction Program is intended to make new homes more affordable in Mississauga and other municipalities. The report says the program is projected to save homebuyers as much as $36,140 per home in construction costs. According to the announcement, buyers of new homes could also receive up to $130,000 in HST relief between April 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027, bringing combined potential savings to as much as $166,140 per home. The funding is tied to the $1.8 billion Build Communities Strong Fund, which the governments say will be distributed over 10 years. According to the report, officials project the program could help unlock 90,000 new homes across the province.

items.title: Don Valley Parkway Reopens After Wednesday's Storm Floods Toronto and Mississauga Streets
items.summary: According to INsauga, heavy rain from Wednesday's severe storm shut down roads and highways across the Greater Toronto Area, including parts of Yonge Street and the Don Valley Parkway. The outlet reports the storm brought torrential rain, large hail and the risk of a tornado to wide swaths of southern Ontario, darkening skies over downtown Toronto and pummelling neighbourhoods farther north with hail. INsauga reports the flooding also suspended subway service during Wednesday's afternoon rush hour, and Toronto police said crews spent Thursday morning clearing debris from the Don Valley Parkway before its southbound lanes reopened. According to the outlet, Credit Valley Conservation issued a flood warning Wednesday evening after the upper watershed received about 70 millimetres of rain, with flooding also reported in Orangeville's First Street, Second Avenue and Rotary Park areas. INsauga reports Peel Regional Police said Bromsgrove Road in Mississauga also flooded, affecting vehicles on the road as well.

items.title: Peel Police Map Nearly 200 Mississauga Auto Thefts Recorded Last Month
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Regional Police recorded nearly 200 auto thefts in Mississauga during August, averaging about six stolen vehicles per day. The outlet reports the August total marked a slight decrease from July, when 206 vehicles were reported stolen in the city. Mississauga.com reports that from January 1 to August 31, a total of 1,624 vehicles were stolen in Mississauga, an 8 per cent decline compared with the 1,765 vehicles stolen over the same period last year. According to the outlet, police have published the theft locations on an interactive crime-mapping tool to help residents see where incidents have occurred. Mississauga.com reports the tool is part of the force's ongoing effort to raise public awareness about auto theft trends in the region.
